§4 Off the stage — he found her, through the manager's reluctant good offices, putting on an undistinguished hat by the aid of a cracked mirror — Hilda Mitchell proved to be an ordinary good-looking person of twenty-five, very weary (Hapgood, who knew the game, expected weariness), very much on her guard, very loath in…
dressed drab in one long, undistinguished gown like a Hicksite or Quaker, without the hood . .
